title: Create a task from the command line
acceptance_criteria: The CLI accepts a task title and optional tag.
Created tasks persist in a local JSON file.
The command prints the created task ID.

title: List persisted tasks
acceptance_criteria: The CLI lists each saved task with its ID, status, title, and tag.
An empty task store produces a clear message.

title: Complete a task from the command line
acceptance_criteria: The CLI accepts a task ID for completion.
Completing an existing open task persists its completed status.
An unknown task ID returns a helpful non-zero error.

title: Add repository code-quality gates
acceptance_criteria: ESLint checks TypeScript source and test files using the current flat configuration format.
The lint gate enforces a maximum file length without duplicating Fallow's complexity checks.
Fallow reports code duplication, cyclomatic and cognitive complexity, dead code, circular dependencies, and large functions.
The repository exposes separate full-codebase and changed-file Fallow commands.
The standard verification command runs type checking, linting, changed-file analysis, and tests.
The verification documentation explains when to run each quality command.

title: Add contract tests for quality gates
acceptance_criteria: An ESLint contract test proves the configured 300-line limit rejects an oversized TypeScript file.
Fallow contract tests prove health analysis detects excessive complexity or function size and duplication analysis detects repeated code.
A clean temporary fixture passes the representative ESLint and Fallow checks.
Fixtures are generated in temporary directories and do not pollute normal source analysis.
Contract tests assert stable exit codes and machine-readable fields instead of human output.
The standard harness verification command runs both product tests and harness contract tests.
Verification documentation explains the two test layers.

title: Document and template the delivery workflow
acceptance_criteria: AGENTS.md contains concise, tool-neutral delivery rules.
docs/run-a-ticket.md explains how to execute a ticket through the harness without repeating long prompts.
A GitHub feature issue form captures the objective, acceptance criteria, verification, and context or risks.
A pull request template captures the linked issue, acceptance criteria, harness reports, verification evidence, and risks.
docs/github-setup.md documents remote ruleset and required-check setup that is not carried by a clone.
The README and completion checkpoints link the workflow from the normal entry points.
The full harness verification passes.

title: Add clear technical prose conventions
acceptance_criteria: docs/conventions.md defines clear technical prose rules based on applicable ASD-STE100 principles.
The convention covers documentation, pull request descriptions, release notes, code comments, issues, and progress reports.
The convention does not claim full ASD-STE100 compliance without validation against the current standard and project terminology.
Commit messages have a separate concise imperative-subject rule.
Chat replies are not included in the repository prose requirement.
AGENTS.md points agents to the prose convention without duplicating it.
Official ASD-STE100 sources are recorded in the documentation.
The full harness verification passes.

title: Add a production-readiness adoption checklist
acceptance_criteria: docs/production-readiness.md provides an adoption checklist.
Each item can be marked applicable, not applicable with a reason, planned with an owner or ticket, or enforced automatically.

The checklist covers correctness and coverage, security, performance, accessibility, domain acceptance, observability, deployment and rollback, data protection and recovery, cost limits, and operational documentation.
The guide asks for a prevented failure, measurable threshold, command, harness integration, required CI check, contract test, and exception owner.
The guide shows the progression from identified risk to required CI gate.
The guide tells adopters to select relevant gates instead of enabling every gate by default.
README.md and AGENTS.md link the checklist from normal adoption and navigation paths.
The full harness verification passes.

title: Make harness completion checkpoints executable
acceptance_criteria: A TypeScript validator checks a repository root and returns all harness-state findings through one small interface.
The validator rejects duplicate or empty feature IDs, invalid statuses, missing titles or acceptance criteria, and more than one active feature in the shared workstream.
An active feature must appear in progress/current.md.
An in_review feature must have an implementation report.
A completed tracked feature must have implementation and review reports and a history entry.
Required reports contain the accepted evidence sections and identify their feature.
Legacy untracked bootstrap features remain valid without fabricated evidence.
The standard harness gate runs the validator before other quality checks.
Contract tests prove valid state passes and representative invalid states fail with stable finding codes.
Verification documentation explains the executable checkpoints and their limits.
The full harness verification passes.

title: Add a fast inner feedback loop
acceptance_criteria: A fast command validates harness state, types, lint rules, changed-file analysis, and product tests.
The full verification command composes the fast command with harness contract tests.
The shell gate invokes the full verification command without duplicate checks.
CI continues to use the shell gate.
Contract tests prevent the fast and full gate definitions from drifting.
Verification documentation explains focused, fast, and full feedback levels.
The full harness verification passes.

title: Document optional parallel worktrees
acceptance_criteria: A guide explains when parallel worktrees are appropriate and when work must remain sequential.
The guide requires one ticket, branch, worktree, and agent per workstream.
The guide uses the issue tracker as the cross-worktree claim mechanism.
The guide provides safe create, inspect, update, and remove commands.
The guide explains queue and progress conflicts when branches converge.
Each worktree retains the standard implementation, review, verification, and pull request gates.
README.md and AGENTS.md link the guide.
The default one-active-feature rule and validator remain unchanged.
The full harness verification passes.

title: Make production-build adoption explicit
acceptance_criteria: A root-level adoption checklist is visible from README.md and AGENTS.md.
The checklist inventories every deployable application and relevant workspace with type-check, test, build, CI, and deployment evidence.
The checklist requires the exact production build for every deployable target.
Verification documentation defines a project-owned verification extension point without imposing one monorepo tool.
The guidance requires a deliberate negative test that proves a broken production build fails the gate.
The guidance covers CI and deployment-provider parity, preview status, and smoke tests where applicable.
The pull request template asks for affected deployable targets and production-build evidence.
Harness contract tests keep the checklist and its primary entry-point links present.
The documentation states that template checks do not prove an adopted project is deployable.
The full harness verification passes.

title: Add a read-only TypeScript adoption audit
acceptance_criteria: A TypeScript interface audits a repository root and returns discovered targets, stable findings, and a proposed inventory.
The audit discovers the root package and packages declared by pnpm-workspace.yaml.
Each target reports its path, package name, TypeScript configuration, frontend indicators, and relevant scripts.
The audit reports missing target inventory, missing project-gate integration, unresolved workspace patterns, and missing commands that need a decision.
The audit does not guess whether a discovered target is deployable.
A CLI prints a readable report and supports machine-readable JSON.
The audit performs no repository writes.
Contract tests use temporary fixtures for a single package, a frontend monorepo, malformed input, and unresolved workspace patterns.
The adoption checklist and verification documentation explain how to use and interpret the audit.
The audit is not part of the standard gate until an adopter approves and configures its proposed inventory.
The full harness verification passes.

title: Validate an approved harness target inventory
acceptance_criteria: harness.targets.json has a versioned and documented schema.
Each target records its path, deployment decision, type-check decision, test decision, and production-build decision.
A decision contains an exact command or a non-applicable reason.
Deployable targets cannot mark the production build as not applicable.
The adoption audit reads the approved inventory and reports malformed, missing, stale, or incomplete entries with stable finding codes.
The audit reports no inventory or deployment-decision finding for a valid declared target.
The bootstrap contains a valid inventory for its sample CLI.
Temporary-fixture contracts cover valid, malformed, missing-target, stale-target, and invalid deployable-build cases.
The adoption checklist and verification guide explain approval and maintenance.
The full harness verification passes.

title: Define a bounded agent repair loop
acceptance_criteria: A repair-loop guide defines observe, diagnose, change, and verify steps.
The default budget permits at most three repair attempts in one repair cycle.
An attempt needs new evidence or a changed hypothesis before another code change.
The protocol forbids rerunning an unchanged deterministic command without a reason.
The protocol defines immediate stop conditions for missing authority, secrets, destructive actions, and ambiguous acceptance criteria.
Exhausted work remains active and is reported as blocked with evidence.
Failed attempts are recorded in the implementation report with command, failure, diagnosis, and result.
AGENTS.md, the implementer role, and the ticket runbook link the protocol without duplicating it.
A harness contract keeps the budget, stop conditions, and entry-point links present.
The documentation states that repository checks cannot detect unreported attempts.
The full harness verification passes.

title: Bind review approval to implementation content
acceptance_criteria: A TypeScript interface computes a deterministic SHA-256 digest from staged repository files.
The digest excludes feature_list.json and progress/ because completion state and the review report change after review.
A command prints the current implementation digest.
Review reports record Implementation digest: sha256:<digest>.
A standard gate validates the report digest for an in_review feature and for the latest completed feature.
A missing, malformed, or stale review digest fails with a stable finding code.
Staged implementation changes after review invalidate the approval.
Documentation requires the implementer to stage intended files before review and the reviewer to recompute the digest.
Temporary Git fixture contracts cover a valid binding, excluded evidence changes, missing binding, and stale binding.
Documentation states that untracked files are outside the digest and must be staged before review.
The full harness verification passes.
